prompt:
ONE original square premium painterly cinematic Mythics illustration of HUITZILOPOCHTLI, the Aztec solar and war deity and patron of Tenochtitlan, depicted as a formidable respected divine presence [huitzilopochtli-c06].
ANATOMY: one humanlike divine warrior, ONE head TWO eyes TWO arms TWO legs. His visible forearms, hands and lower legs are painted BLUE [huitzilopochtli-c21]. Opaque high-neck woven ceremonial tunic with sleeves to the elbows covers shoulders, chest, abdomen and upper thighs; secure opaque lower garments, no bare torso or thighs. A fitted helmet carries a clearly bounded fan of HUMMINGBIRD FEATHERS, with its whole silhouette visible inside the frame [huitzilopochtli-c22]. His RIGHT hand holds one substantial SNAKE-SHAPED SPEAR-THROWER, an atlatl representing the FIRE SERPENT XIUHCOATL. It is a real carved serpent-shaped handheld weapon, not a sword or loose giant animal. His LEFT hand holds one plain round SHIELD. These weapon and shield attributes are documented [huitzilopochtli-c21]. Exactly two hands; no additional weapons, hands or wings.
MOMENT: he leans forward at the top of a temple stair, thrusting the physical snake-shaped atlatl diagonally toward the close camera with his right hand; his left hand holds the shield raised beside his body. Head and complete hummingbird feather helmet face the viewer, blue-painted wrists and hands grip two separate attributes securely. The action is a forceful divine arrival without a target or victim.
POWER: real fire burns from the serpent head of the hand-held FIRE SERPENT WEAPON [huitzilopochtli-c02] and singes the edge of a foreground stone stair, producing sparks and thin smoke. The solar deity context is literal dying sunlight over the distant city [huitzilopochtli-c06]; no energy serpent, laser or aura.
SCALE & CAMERA: extremely close low oblique waist-up perspective with atlatl serpent-head silhouette large in the lower foreground, face and full helmet centered above; shield clearly separate on the other side. The composition differs from a full-body rocky mountaintop view: tight forward temple-stair confrontation. No extra limbs or hidden attribute hands.
LIGHT & WEATHER: dominant orange-red weapon fire lights face and blue hands; dim sunset light only in background; thin soot smoke, warm dark shadows.
SETTING: atop Temple Mayor with Tenochtitlan faintly visible behind his shoulder, from his documented shrine [huitzilopochtli-c16]. Stone architecture has plain undecorated surfaces without inscriptions or modern national flag.
SURFACE: tactile woven cloth, blue body paint over real skin on forearms/hands/shins, aged wood and bronze on the atlatl and shield, iridescent small hummingbird feathers, dark volcanic rock and ember soot. Rich painterly brushwork, dark walnut and antique gold with deep blue and one orange-red fire accent.
MOOD: awe-inspiring divine authority, powerful focused gaze and purposeful movement, respectful to indigenous tradition. Never a generic masked soldier, ordinary man, cute character or monstrous caricature.
HARD CONSTRAINTS: no text, writing, pseudo-glyphs, logo, border, frame, watermark or signature; no gore, severed heads, corpses, sacrifices, victims or attacking people; no nude torso; no extra heads, eyes, arms, legs or fingers; no generic glowing aura, neon outlines, energy ribbons, floating runes; no modern gun, European armor, sword, mechanical armor or design borrowed from games, films, anime or comics. The burning weapon must remain a physical snake-shaped atlatl in his hand, without a separate giant serpent creature.
